answer: Each identity registers one trellis in a karst garden, staking a 65-credit bond and filing its span and the plot drip rate. The board publishes a karst flow table mapping rainfall to drip; an auditor recomputes each filing and burns the bond on deviation over 5%, a reused plot, or a duplicate trellis. The first filing costs 33 credits, the kth 33+9(k-1), the 1000th 9024, so 1000 fakes cost 4,528,500 plus 65,000 locked. A rented-trellis ring fails: each trellis is key-bound to its first filer, so a second filing collides. An honest gardener pays 33 once and recovers the bond after audit.
